title: U.S. Senate · Montana

context.text: This is an open seat. On March 4, 2026, incumbent Sen. Steve Daines (R) withdrew his candidacy and endorsed Kurt Alme, who filed to run the same day; Seth Bodnar also filed as an independent that day. According to Montana Free Press, this makes the race the first Montana U.S. Senate election without an incumbent running in 40 years. Alme, Alani Bankhead and Bodnar are viewed as the leading candidates. On July 8, 2026, 17 Democratic state legislators publicly asked Bankhead and Bodnar to decide which of them would end their campaign, warning a split vote could help Republicans; neither withdrew, and the deadline to withdraw from the ballot passed on August 10, 2026, so both remain on the ballot.

candidates.name: Kurt Alme
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary on June 2, 2026; entered the race March 4, 2026 after Sen. Steve Daines withdrew and endorsed him.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana (Oct. 2025–March 2026)

summary.text: Kurt Alme is the Republican nominee for the open Montana U.S. Senate seat. He is an attorney who served as U.S. Attorney for Montana, budget director under Gov. Greg Gianforte, and director of the Montana Department of Revenue under Gov. Judy Martz, before entering the race when Sen. Steve Daines withdrew and endorsed him.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Colorado in 1989 and a law degree from Harvard Law School in 1992.
Was a partner at the law firm Crowley Fleck.
Served as director of the Montana Department of Revenue under Gov. Judy Martz (R) and as budget director under Gov. Greg Gianforte (R).
Served as U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana from October 7, 2025 until leaving office on March 4, 2026 to run for Senate.

priorities.text: Says he is running to protect veterans, defend the Second Amendment, keep transgender girls and women out of women's and girls' sports, support farmers and ranchers, protect public lands, and secure elections.
Says he has a record of cutting taxes, balancing the state budget and prosecuting violent crime.
priorities.quote: I’m the only candidate up here with a proven record of cutting taxes, balancing our state budget, and locking up violent criminals,

priorities.text: Says he would work for affordability, safer communities and the Montana way of life.
priorities.quote: make our lives more affordable, make our communities safer, and protect our Montana way of life.

candidates.researchNotes: Priorities page on almeforsenate.com contains placeholder text. Quotes are from the Oct. 11, 2026 debate as reported by the Daily Montanan; the Daily Montanan reports he has declined other debate invitations. No quotes found on abortion, guns, immigration or tariffs.

statements.quote: We need to hold them accountable, and we need to make healthcare more affordable by making it more transparent, more competitive, and by putting patients first,
statements.context: In the Oct. 11, 2026 Bozeman debate, per the Daily Montanan, after saying the Affordable Care Act subsidized drug and insurance companies

candidates.name: Alani Bankhead
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026.

summary.text: Alani Bankhead is the Democratic nominee for the open Montana U.S. Senate seat. She is a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and counterintelligence agent who later founded a life-coaching company, running on housing, healthcare and government accountability.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and Latin American studies from Pennsylvania State University in 2004 and a graduate degree from Troy University in 2012.
Served in the U.S. Air Force from 2004, working as a counterintelligence agent and rising to lieutenant colonel over roughly 21 years of service.
Founded a life-coaching company called Mighty Sparrow Coaching.

priorities.text: Running on housing, healthcare, and government accountability.
"After 21 years of serving, I was looking at my beautiful state and country burning and I knew I had a special set of skills to offer the people of Montana."

positions.summary: In her Ballotpedia survey she names reproductive freedom as a policy priority and says Montanans wrote it into the state constitution.
positions.quote: Reproductive freedom - Montanans already wrote it into our constitution, and Washington keeps trying to override them.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she will protect the Medicare and Medicaid payments rural hospitals depend on and protect and properly fund Medicaid long-term care.
positions.quote: We will keep those doors open — by protecting the Medicare and Medicaid payments they depend on, and paying for it by cutting Washington’s waste, not Montana’s care.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would remove the Social Security wage cap so the wealthiest pay in on all their income.
positions.quote: Fund Social Security for good by removing the wage cap so the wealthiest pay in on all their income

candidates.researchNotes: Basic-tier research from Ballotpedia; no personal campaign website or additional issue statements located in the time available.

candidates.name: Seth Bodnar
candidates.ballotNote: Filed as an independent on March 4, 2026, the same day Sen. Steve Daines withdrew.
candidates.currentRole: Former president of the University of Montana

summary.text: Seth Bodnar is an independent candidate for the open Montana U.S. Senate seat. He is a former Green Beret, General Electric executive and University of Montana president who argues both major parties have failed the state.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the United States Military Academy at West Point and two master's degrees from the University of Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar and Truman Scholar.
Served as a Green Beret in the U.S. Army beginning in 1997.
Worked as a manager and executive at General Electric.
Served as president of the University of Montana.

priorities.text: "This country is in crisis, and our national political parties are failing us. Montanans are an independent people, and they deserve an independent voice fighting for them in Washington, DC. I'm not a politician, I'm a soldier, a businessman, a husband, a father."
Ending the war in Iran, citing Congress's authority over war.
priorities.quote: END THE COSTLY AND UNAUTHORIZED WAR IN IRAN

priorities.text: Lowering health care premiums and drug costs.
priorities.quote: LOWER HEALTH CARE PREMIUMS AND DRUG COSTS

priorities.text: Making it more affordable to buy a home.
priorities.quote: MAKE IT MORE AFFORDABLE TO BUY A HOME

positions.summary: Campaign site lists reasserting Congress's authority to declare war before troops are committed to combat.
positions.quote: Reasserting Congress's constitutional authority to declare war before American troops are committed to combat.

positions.summary: Campaign site supports targeted tariffs as leverage and opposes blanket tariffs on allies such as Canada.
positions.quote: Support targeted, strategic tariffs used as leverage against countries actually cheating on trade, not blanket tariffs on allies like Canada.

positions.summary: Campaign site lists defending Medicaid expansion and an affordable coverage option for every American.
positions.quote: Defending Medicaid expansion, which has helped keep every rural hospital in Montana open.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he opposes a federal assault weapons ban, a new universal background check mandate and a federal red-flag law.
positions.quote: Seth opposes a federal assault weapons ban, a new universal background check mandate, and a federal red-flag law.

positions.summary: Campaign site lists codifying Roe v. Wade into federal law.
positions.quote: Codifying Roe v. Wade into federal law.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he opposes school vouchers.
positions.quote: Seth will oppose school vouchers that siphon public tax dollars to private schools.

positions.summary: Campaign site lists zoning and code reform that expands housing supply.
positions.quote: Cutting the red tape slowing new housing construction and support zoning and code reform that expands supply.

candidates.researchNotes: From the issues page of his campaign site (sethformontana.com/issues; each topic expands to a list of what he supports). Page is undated; it refers to the Iran war and 2026 events. He did not take a position on the wording of the guide's immigration-enforcement or tax statements, so those appear as statements only.

statements.quote: Enforcing the immigration laws already on the books.
statements.context: On his campaign site, under 'Secure our border and enforce immigration laws'

statements.quote: Strengthening long-term solvency through fairer contributions from the highest earners.
statements.context: On his campaign site, under 'Protect Social Security and Medicare'

candidates.name: Kyle Austin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party primary on June 2, 2026; previously a Libertarian candidate in 2022 and 2024.

summary.text: Kyle Austin is the Libertarian Party nominee for the open Montana U.S. Senate seat. He is a pharmacist and founder of the pharmacy company Pharm406.

background.text: Born in Havre, Montana, and graduated from Havre High School in 2001.
Earned a doctorate in pharmacy from the University of Montana Pharmacy School in 2008.
Worked as a pharmacist and founded his own company, Pharm406.

priorities.text: Agriculture, drawing on his family farm.
priorities.quote: Austin understands the stress, the challenges, and the problems our American farmers and ranchers face.
Austin is a gun owner, and a hunter understands the importance of gun rights in America.

priorities.text: A healthcare plan he calls Healthcare 2.0, drawing on his work as a pharmacist.
priorities.quote: Austin, as a pharmacist and pharmacy owner, understands the healthcare issues and corruption related to the healthcare industry.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he believes everyone should have unrestricted access to bear arms.
positions.quote: Austin believes everyone American should un-restricted access to bear arms.

candidates.researchNotes: From his campaign homepage (third-person text, quote as published) and the Oct. 11, 2026 debate coverage. His platform page did not load. No quotes found on other guide issues.

statements.quote: to create one set of rules, to get the payers to clean up their mess and actually pay our providers what they’re worth.
statements.context: In the Oct. 11, 2026 Bozeman debate, describing his 'Healthcare 2.0' plan, per the Daily Montanan
